data.title: Redirect
data.tagline: A redirect is a mechanism that sends a visit from one URL to another URL.
data.learningOutcome: You can decide where an old URL should go and distinguish a real redirect from client-side routing or a rewrite.
data.description: When a product is renamed, an old link can automatically lead to its matching new address; after sign-in, a page may also return someone to what they meant to view. A redirect changes the destination URL. It is not merely an in-page view change, and unrelated old content should not all be sent to the home page.

learning.assumes: You have followed an old link that automatically opened a new page or seen a 404 page.
learning.outcome: You can decide where an old URL should go and distinguish a real redirect from client-side routing or a rewrite.

explanation.title: The request reaches the old address first
explanation.text: After a browser visits an old URL, a server or hosting platform returns a new destination address; the browser requests it and the address bar usually reflects the new URL.

explanation.title: A destination should truly correspond
explanation.text: Page migrations, domain changes, and post-login return paths need a clear destination. When the content matches, people keep the context they came for.

data.boundary: A redirect is not the same as internal routing in a single-page app or a server rewrite. Internal routing can update an interface in one app; a rewrite can retain the original address. A redirect explicitly takes a visitor to another URL.

lessonPractice.title: The old `/account` URL must permanently lead to `/settings/profile`, and the address bar must show the new URL. What should be done?

options.label: Configure a redirect to the new URL, then visit the old URL and check the final address and content
options.feedback: Correct. A redirect makes the browser continue to the new URL, so both the address bar and content should show the new target.

options.label: Return the profile page content at the old URL while keeping `/account` in the address bar
options.feedback: That is closer to a server rewrite: the content changes, but the browser is not taken to the new URL.

options.label: Open the old page and switch its internal state to the profile section without changing the URL
options.feedback: An in-page state change does not migrate the old URL or make the address bar show the new target.

data.agentPrompt: Redirect the old `/pricing-2025` address to `/pricing`, handling only this confirmed matching pair. Then visit the old address directly and confirm the address bar reaches the new URL, the page is not a 404, and there is no redirect loop.
